sections.title: Growth, Profitability & Cash Generation
sections.subtitle: GAAP net income is distorted by one-off items (FY2024 tax release, Q2-2026 Delivery Hero mark-to-market gain) -- operating income and FCF are the cleaner signals

charts.title: Net Income vs Operating Income vs FCF
charts.annotation: Net income swings on non-operating items unrelated to the business: a ~$6.4bn FY2024 deferred-tax release, a $1.6bn Q4-2025 equity mark-to-market hit ($296m net income on $1.77bn operating income), and a Q2-2026 'other income' of +$1,342m that includes ~$1.1bn from an equity-securities remeasurement tied to the pending Delivery Hero stake. Operating income and FCF track the underlying business; net income does not.

charts.title: EBITDA (FY basis)
charts.annotation: Interim EBITDA is not reliably disclosed for every recent quarter, so this chart is FY-only. FY2025 EBITDA of $8,730m rose from $2,782m in FY2023 as the platform scaled past fixed technology and G&A costs.

sections.title: Platform Scale & Segment Mix
sections.subtitle: Gross bookings, active consumers and the three-segment revenue split -- segment profitability is not comparable pre/post the Q1-2026 measure change

charts.title: Gross Bookings per Monthly Active Consumer
charts.annotation: A proxy for platform monetization per user, not a company-disclosed metric -- Uber reports take rate and Uber One membership separately but not this ratio directly. Rising steadily as Uber One penetration (>36m members, ~60% YoY growth) and multi-product usage (rides + eats + grocery) deepen spend per consumer.

sections.title: Capital Structure & Balance Sheet
sections.subtitle: The Delivery Hero bridge facility is the key forward risk: a levered balance sheet ahead of a 2H-2027 close

charts.title: Cash & Equivalents vs Total Debt
charts.annotation: Debt rose from $10,521m (FY2025) to $12,723m and cash fell from $7,105m to $4,870m by Q2-2026 -- the balance-sheet impact of pre-funding the ~EUR14.2bn Delivery Hero acquisition bridge. Net debt is now $7,853m against a near-net-cash position a year ago.

charts.title: Shares Outstanding & Stock-Based Comp
charts.annotation: Shares fell from 2,150.5m (FY2024) to 2,119.7m (FY2025) to 2,042.6m (Q2-2026) as the $20bn buyback authorization (announced Q2-2025, $3bn repurchased in Q1-2026 alone) outpaces SBC-driven issuance.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Capex
charts.annotation: Capex is small and shrinking relative to operating cash flow ($135m capex against $5,213m H1-2026 OCF, ~2.6%) -- Uber's asset-light marketplace model means almost all operating cash converts to free cash flow, unlike capital-intensive AV or logistics operators.

revenue.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
revenue.content:
Total reported revenue and its year-over-year growth rate.

For Uber: Revenue reached $52.0bn in FY2025 (+19% YoY) and Q2-2026 revenue was $14,191m, +12.2% YoY. Growth has decelerated from the >80% pandemic-recovery years to a mid-teens/low-double-digit steady state as the base has scaled.

What to watch:

  • Whether growth stabilizes in the low-to-mid teens as guided (18-22% constant-currency gross bookings growth implies some FX drag on reported USD revenue)
  • Revenue take-rate mix shift as advertising and Uber One monetization scale ahead of gross bookings

operatingMargin.title: Operating Income & Margin
operatingMargin.content:
GAAP income from operations and operating margin (operating income / revenue) -- the cleanest read on underlying platform profitability, unaffected by equity mark-to-market noise below the operating line.

For Uber: Q2-2026 operating income was $1,890m (+30% YoY) on $14,191m revenue, and H1-2026 operating income grew 42% YoY -- operating leverage is running well ahead of revenue growth. FY2025 operating income was $5,565m (10.7% margin), up from $2,799m (6.4% margin) in FY2024.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin expansion continues as driver/courier incentive costs scale sub-linearly with gross bookings
  • Any AV-related cost drag as Uber Autonomous Solutions scales city deployments in 2026

niVsFcf.title: Net Income vs Operating Income vs FCF
niVsFcf.content:
GAAP net income against operating income and reported free cash flow -- deliberately shown together because net income has been an unreliable earnings signal for Uber across several recent periods.

For Uber: Q2-2026 'other income, net' was +$1,342m, including +$1,618m of equity-securities gains, roughly $1.1bn of which was a one-off remeasurement tied to the pending Delivery Hero transaction -- yet H1-2026 'other income' overall was actually NEGATIVE $152m once other marks are netted. FY2024 net income of $9.86bn included a ~$6.4bn one-off deferred-tax-valuation-allowance release. Q4-2025 net income was just $296m against $1.77bn of operating income on an equity mark-to-market swing. Operating income and FCF are the metrics to trust for trend; net income is not.

What to watch:

  • Further equity-investment mark-to-market swings (Didi, Grab, Aurora, Wayve, Delivery Hero stake) continuing to distort quarterly net income
  • Operating income and FCF continuing to compound while net income stays noisy -- a widening, not narrowing, gap is expected and not a red flag by itself

ebitda.title: EBITDA (FY basis)
ebitda.content:
Reported EBITDA at each fiscal year-end. Shown FY-only because interim-quarter EBITDA is not consistently disclosed in the underlying filings for every recent period.

For Uber: FY2025 EBITDA was $8,730m, more than triple the $2,782m reported in FY2023, as the platform crossed into sustained scale profitability. Note Uber's segment profitability measure changed in Q1-2026 from Segment Adjusted EBITDA to Segment Operating Income -- this consolidated EBITDA line is a separate, still-comparable company-level figure, not the redefined segment measure.

What to watch:

  • Continued EBITDA margin expansion as a share of gross bookings
  • Any divergence between this consolidated EBITDA and segment-level operating income as the AV and advertising businesses scale

bookings.title: Gross Bookings & YoY Growth
bookings.content:
Total dollar value of rides, deliveries and freight booked on the platform before Uber's take -- the top-line demand metric management guides on, distinct from revenue (which reflects only Uber's commission).

For Uber: FY2025 gross bookings were $193.5bn (+19% YoY). Q2-2026 guidance called for 18-22% constant-currency growth; reported-currency growth typically runs a few points below that on dollar strength.

What to watch:

  • Constant-currency vs reported-currency growth gap as a read on FX headwind, given ~46% of revenue is international
  • Gross bookings growth relative to revenue growth as a read on blended take-rate trend

mapcs.title: Monthly Active Platform Consumers & Trips
mapcs.content:
Monthly Active Platform Consumers (MAPCs) -- unique users who completed a ride or order in the trailing month -- and total trips completed on the platform.

For Uber: MAPCs reached 202m at FY2025/Q4-2025 (+18% YoY), and trips reached 13.6bn for FY2025 (+20% YoY). Uber One membership exceeded 36m by mid-2025, growing ~60% YoY and driving disproportionate bookings and frequency.

What to watch:

  • Trips-per-MAPC as a frequency/engagement signal, since it is more resilient to macro pullbacks than new-user growth
  • Uber One penetration continuing to outpace overall MAPC growth

segmentRevenue.title: Segment Revenue: Mobility, Delivery, Freight
segmentRevenue.content:
Revenue split across Uber's three reportable segments.

For Uber: FY2025: Mobility $29.67bn (~57%, +21% YoY), Delivery $17.25bn (~33%), Freight $5.10bn (~10%, broadly flat). Freight remains a thin-margin, low-growth drag on the overall mix; Mobility and Delivery both continue to grow at double digits. Note: the Q1-2026 measure change from Segment Adjusted EBITDA to Segment Operating Income affects segment PROFITABILITY comparability, not this revenue split.

What to watch:

  • Delivery share of mix continuing to climb as grocery/alcohol/convenience categories scale beyond core restaurant delivery
  • Freight's persistently thin contribution to consolidated profitability

bookingsPerConsumer.title: Gross Bookings per Monthly Active Consumer
bookingsPerConsumer.content:
Gross bookings divided by monthly active platform consumers -- a derived proxy for spend intensity per user, not a figure Uber discloses directly (the company reports take rate and Uber One membership separately).

For Uber: This ratio has risen steadily as multi-product usage (rides plus Eats plus grocery) and Uber One membership (which drives 3.4x higher spend per member) deepen engagement per consumer, independent of new-user growth.

What to watch:

  • This is a derived ratio, not a disclosed KPI -- treat trend direction as informative, the absolute level as approximate
  • Any deceleration would suggest new-user growth, not deepening engagement, is doing the work of gross-bookings growth

debtCash.title: Cash & Equivalents vs Total Debt
debtCash.content:
Balance-sheet cash and equivalents against total debt outstanding.

For Uber: Net debt jumped from roughly $3.4bn at FY2025 to $7,853m by Q2-2026 as Uber began pre-funding the pending Delivery Hero acquisition (~EUR41.50/share, ~$14.8bn) via a EUR14.2bn bridge facility ahead of the deal's expected 2H-2027 close. Debt rose $10,521m to $12,723m while cash fell $7,105m to $4,870m in the same period.

What to watch:

  • This is the single largest identified forward balance-sheet risk: bridge-to-term refinancing terms, and whether the Delivery Hero deal closes on schedule or is repriced/renegotiated
  • Net debt trajectory through the 2H-2027 close -- further increases would signal the deal is being funded more with debt than free cash flow

shares.title: Shares Outstanding & Stock-Based Comp
shares.content:
Fully diluted shares outstanding at each fiscal year-end, against annual stock-based compensation expense.

For Uber: Shares fell from 2,150.5m (FY2024) to 2,119.7m (FY2025) to 2,042.6m (Q2-2026) as the $20bn buyback authorization (announced Q2-2025) outpaces SBC-driven dilution -- $3bn was repurchased in Q1-2026 alone. SBC itself has been roughly flat in dollar terms ($1.8-1.9bn/year) even as revenue has grown, so it is a shrinking percentage of revenue.

What to watch:

  • Whether buyback pace is maintained once the Delivery Hero cash outlay begins, given the balance sheet is already levering up for that deal
  • SBC as a % of revenue continuing to decline as the denominator grows faster than the numerator

capex.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Capex
capex.content:
Cash generated from operations against capital expenditure -- the two disclosed inputs to free cash flow.

For Uber: H1-2026 operating cash flow was $5,213m against just $135m of capex (~2.6%), leaving $5,078m of free cash flow, +7.5% YoY. Uber's asset-light marketplace model -- it owns neither the vehicles nor, for now, the AV fleets its partners operate -- means capex intensity stays structurally low even as the business scales, unlike capital-heavy logistics or AV-fleet-owner peers.

What to watch:

  • Whether capex intensity stays low as Uber Autonomous Solutions scales -- if Uber ever takes fleet ownership risk rather than staying a pure marketplace, this ratio would change materially
  • Working-capital timing (deferred bookings, driver payable float) as a source of OCF volatility quarter to quarter, distinct from the capex line itself

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case Year-1 revenue/FCF growth (12%), decelerating to 8% by Year 4, below the 17.7% revenue 3-year CAGR
